Subject: Re: Private maintenance: planned security patch + rollback readiness

Hi Lara —

Thanks for the heads up. Attaching our preflight checklist and a condensed contingency matrix. Short answers up front:

1) Version pinning: we pin at three layers — model artifact (SHA), runtime package (Deb/RPM artifact ID), and deployment manifest (config map with explicit image tag + checksum). The rollback-script.sh we included re-applies the last known-good manifest and forces KV-cache invalidation to avoid stale embeddings/kv state.

2) Network changes: for this patch we *do not* touch firewall/NAT rules. We will only cordon and drain nodes, and if a control-plane change is required we follow your change freeze window and run a pre-approved firewall policy which we will pre-stage in a disabled state. Any enabled change requires explicit sign-off from FinBank SOC.

3) SLA for rollback: our canary strategy runs on 10% of capacity for 30 minutes with health checks (qps, p99 latency, error-rate, and correctness spot-checks). If any of the canary checks fail we execute the circuit-breaker: automatic rollback + network route revert and a hot warm-up of pinned nodes. Target RTO in that scenario is 20–30 minutes; we will rehearse once in staging with your ops team before the window.

Attached: preflight_checklist.pdf (2 pages), network-topology-v2.drawio (diagram), rollback-script.sh (script stub).

Planned maintenance window suggestion: Saturday 2026-05-09 02:00–05:00 UTC. If that works we will run a gating rehearsal on 2026-05-02 in your staging environment.

Next steps (action items):
- Lara: confirm maintenance window and SOC point-of-contact for the runbook (name + pager)
- Hannah/Priyom: coordinate canary rehearsal schedule with FinBank staging
- Marcus: validate rollback script lines 42–62 with infra team (KV cache invalidation)

Connor O'Brien
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private maintenance: planned security patch + rollback readiness

Lara / team —

We can run the rehearsal in staging on May 2. Quick notes from the ops side:
- Canary config: 10% traffic split using smart routing; synthetic traffic generator + a small set of regression prompts from FinBank will run every 5m during the canary.
- Health gates: we gate on (1) p99 CPU < 70% for the host, (2) error rate < 0.5%, (3) end-to-end correctness score on the prompt set not regressing > 2% absolute.
- Escape hatches: immediate 'circuit-breaker' k8s taint + route swap to backup pool (we'll prepare the alternate pool in the same AZs to minimize cross-region latency).

I'll validate the rollback-script.sh lines Marcus flagged and add a short step to rotate KMS keys only if absolutely required; otherwise keys remain untouched.

Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
